Saint Natalia of Rome, also known as Saint Nataliana, was a Christian martyr who lived in the late 1st or early 2nd century AD. According to tradition, she was a noblewoman from Rome who was married to a pagan soldier named Publius. After Publius was killed in battle, Natalia was approached by a group of Christian missionaries who asked her to convert to their faith. She was initially reluctant, but eventually agreed and was baptized. However, her conversion was not kept a secret for long, and she was denounced to the Roman authorities by her former servants. Natalia is venerated as the patron saint of those who are persecuted for their faith and those who experience difficulties in marriage.
